blocks.text: All chemical reactions involve the breaking of bonds in the reactant molecules before new bonds form, which can happen only if the reactant molecules collide with enough energy to overcome an energy barrier.

blocks.title: Energy of activation
blocks.text: The minimum amount of energy required by the reactant molecules just to cross the energy barrier is the energy of activation, Ea.

blocks.alt: Two energy profiles, Enthalpy against Progress of Reaction. Left (exothermic): a red curve rises from the reactants level HR to a peak and falls to the lower products level HP; a dashed arrow Ea goes from HR up to the peak and a solid arrow delta H goes from HR down to HP. Right (endothermic): the curve rises from HR (reactants, low) to a peak and falls to HP (products, higher); a dashed arrow Ea from HR to the peak and an arrow delta H from HR up to HP.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.2: Energy profile diagram in terms of delta H and Ea (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.2).
